# Vendored Mutable Instruments code

This directory holds the DSP of Mutable Instruments **Beads**, designed and written by Émilie Gillet, plus the reverb, diffuser and pitch-shifter classes of Mutable Instruments **Clouds** (same author) and the subset of Mutable's **stmlib** they depend on. Particules (granular mode), Retours (delay mode) and Ondes (wavetable voice) run on Beads; Brume runs on the Beads and Clouds reverbs and the Clouds diffuser and pitch shifter.

- Upstream: <https://github.com/pichenettes/eurorack>, Beads source released in commit `d8f473915232af74347762b6365202bfd26f73f6` (vendored from `f4cfa7697095a28d292bff758beb51deb49b5a86`, identical `beads/` tree). The Clouds files come from the same commit: `clouds/dsp/frame.h` and `clouds/dsp/fx/{fx_engine,reverb,diffuser,pitch_shifter}.h`.
- stmlib submodule: `e3bd7c9cc00e4364166f9905c0509b6ffd0535ec`.
- Licence: MIT (see `LICENSE`, copied from stmlib; the Beads files carry the same notice in their headers).

## Local changes

All local changes are in `robotboy.patch` and are marked `// RobotBoy:` in the source. `update.sh /path/to/eurorack` recreates this directory from upstream and re-applies the patch.

1. `Processor` can pin granular or delay mode (`set_mode_lock`) instead of following the Size knob, skip the reverb (`set_reverb_enabled`), clear the active buffer (`ClearBuffer`), and report its active grain count (`num_active_grains`) and the per-frame gate of the last block (`gate_out`).
2. `Parameters::pitch_lock`: an optional quantizer applied to each grain's pitch, in semitones, when the grain starts.
3. The packed 12-bit delay-line items force the GCC bitfield layout on MinGW, and every item size is checked with a `static_assert`.
4. `Tap` skips the delay-line reads of a tap whose gain is zero (it still advances its pitch-shifter phase). The output is bit-identical; delay mode costs much less CPU, because most of its 16 taps are silent at any moment.
5. `stmlib.h` defines `M_PI` when a strict `-std=c++20` C library (MetaModule's newlib) hides it.
6. Read-only accessors for Lucarne's grain display: the delay line's write pointer and samples, each grain's position, speed, stereo position, envelope level, length and a per-slot start counter, and the active granular processor (`Processor::VisitGranular`). The output is bit-identical.
7. Tap and play-head accessors for Lucarne's Retours view (read-only).
8. `Reverb` sleeps: when the send is exactly 0, both filter states are exactly 0 and the last full pass over its memory wrote only zeros, it skips the tank and keeps only the level glides, write pointer and LFOs moving (`FxEngine::Advance`). The output is bit-identical, so it only saves CPU while Reverb is at 0 and the tail has decayed to nothing. Needs flush-to-zero (as VCV Rack sets it) for the tape media to reach sleep; without it a filter state sticks at the smallest denormal and the reverb just keeps running.
9. Beads `Reverb`: `set_diffusion` (default 0.625), `set_lfo_rate` (scales the two LFOs without restarting their phase) and `set_mod_depth` (default 1, scales the modulation excursions), for Brume. At the defaults the stock code path runs and the output is bit-identical. `FxEngine::SetLFOFrequencyKeepPhase` and `CosineOscillator::SetFrequencyKeepPhase` (stmlib) support it: the oscillator is re-seeded at its current phase with the standard amplitude, so the LFO stays within [0, 1]. `FxEngine::lfo_value` and `Reverb::lfo_value` are read-only accessors. `set_size` (default 1, clamped to 0.5 .. 2) scales every delay length; a new size glides linearly across the next block. `set_force_custom` keeps the reverb on the variable-driven path for good. That path reads every delay at its stock length times the size, interpolated (exact at size 1, where the offsets are whole), and its layout has room for 2x size with 4x modulation depth (`set_mod_depth` clamps to 4; the excursions do not scale with the size): `ap1`'s smear write and tail move further along the line together, so at size 1 the allpass keeps its stock delay, and every other line grows. `static_assert`s check the room. The `FxEngine` grows from 32768 to 65536 words, so Particules and Retours allocate 64 KB more reverb memory; the stock path's reads and writes are relative to the write pointer, so its output is unchanged, but sleep, which waits for a full pass over the memory, now starts after 65536 silent samples instead of 32768. `reverb.h` includes `fx_engine.h` with `-Wunused-local-typedefs` silenced (its `STATIC_ASSERT`s expand to unused typedefs).
10. Clouds `Reverb`: `set_lfo_rate` (upstream hardcodes 32 kHz), `set_mod_depth` and `Clear` (empties the memory and both filter states, which upstream leaves uninitialized); `set_size` and `set_force_custom` with the same 2x size, 4x depth layout (every line, `del1`'s tail read included), for which its `FxEngine` grows from 16384 to 65536 words; `Diffuser::Clear` and `Diffuser::set_diffusion` (default 0.625); the same `FxEngine` additions. At the default depth, unforced, the output matches upstream bit for bit: the stock layout's reads and writes are relative to the write pointer, so it runs unchanged in the larger memory. `PitchShifter` is unchanged.

## Build notes

- Compile with `-DTEST` (selects stmlib's portable `Clip16`/`Sqrt` instead of ARM inline assembly, as VCV's Audible Instruments does) and `-Dstmlib=robotboy_stmlib -Dclouds=robotboy_clouds` (keep these stmlib and Clouds symbols from colliding with other Mutable ports linked into the same binary, such as the MetaModule simulator or Audible Instruments' Clouds).
- `synth.cc`, `wavetable_granular_player.h` and `wavetable_grain.h` are vendored for completeness; only the wavetable tables and `wavetable_voice.h` are used (by Ondes).
